newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities up but off highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were firmer but off highs in late trade as the battered underlying markets bounced off midsession lows, dealers said.
Overall option volume was light as caution reigned ahead of the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, they added.
"We seemed to have recaptured a little bit of the bid that we lost late last week," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. "But it's been a fairly quiet day volatility-wise."

Implied volatility for CBOT June Treasury bond futures options stood at about 9.5 percent shortly before the close, up from Friday's closing at around 9.3 percent but off highs near 9.7 percent earlier in the day.
Traders said even the bond market's afternoon bounce reflected to some degree the market's nervousness about taking positions ahead of the FOMC meeting.
"I think it was just position-squaring," the CBOT trader said of the late upmove in bond prices.
Traders said most of the larger option deals today were done either delta-neutral or with very small directional bias.

Activity in April CBOT T-bond options, which expire at the end of the week, was largely confined to position adjustments, although an investment bank was seen buying 2,000 contracts of April 108 puts.
April contracts have high gamma and are very responsive to movement in bond prices, but time decay was too severe to attract strong bids as the FOMC meeting was still more than a week away.
Dealers said gamma traders prefered to set themselves up for FOMC with May options, perhaps toward the end of the week when market-makers take the weekend decay out of premiums.

Traders said Wednesday's February consumer price index could be the most important event this week as a strong reading in CPI would make it easier for Fed chairman Alan Greenspan to make a credit-tightening decision at FOMC.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Eurodollar volatilities were generally firmer as futures sagged.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options firmed a quarter point each to about 11.3 and 13.4 percent.

Front-month futures were seen to have priced in a 25 basis point tightening at least halfway, but traders said contracts for September and beyond would have much more room to slide if the Fed did raise rates and raised the specter of further tightening later in the year.
"Vols usually come off after an event," one trader said. "But with the first rate hike of a cycle, that might not be the case."
